raw_response:
I've been farming these 3 mu for 50 years now. My father taught me when I was young, and I've done it ever since. I'm 71 this year, my back isn't what it used to be, but I still manage with my wife's help. My son and his wife work at a factory in Handan — they send some money home, but I can't ask them for farming money. We have to make do with what we have.

This year, I'll do wheat-maize double crop on all 3 mu, same as always. That's the only way to feed the family.

For wheat, I always plant around October 10th. That's when everyone in the village plants, and it's always worked for me. I buy the improved seed from the old shop in town — it's about 12-13 kg per mu, costs around 40 yuan. I know some people use fancy hybrids now, but I've been using this seed for years and it works. I till the field after maize harvest with the small rotary tiller my nephew helps me with.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer before planting — about 35-40 jin per mu (that's around 18-20 kg). It has some nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium all together. Then in March, when the wheat turns green, I topdress with urea — about 20 jin per mu (10 kg). Some years I add a bit more at jointing if the wheat looks yellow, but that costs more, so I usually stick to two times. In total, it's about 15-16 kg of nitrogen per mu.

Irrigation — I do three times. First right after planting so the seeds sprout well. Second before winter freeze, around late November. Third at jointing in April. Water from the well costs money to pump — about 15 yuan each time per mu — but you can't skip it. A dry wheat field means no harvest.

I spray herbicide once in spring. The weeds get bad if you don't. No insecticide usually — the wheat doesn't get too many bugs around here.

For maize, we plant immediately after wheat harvest, around June 12-15. The window is tight — sometimes only 3-4 days. I don't till much, just plant the maize seeds directly into the wheat stubble. I buy hybrid maize seed — about 2 jin per mu, costs more, around 60 yuan, but the yield is better than saving your own seed for maize.

For maize fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer at planting, about the same as wheat. Then at the big喇叭口 stage, if it hasn't rained much, I add some urea. Maybe 10-12 kg nitrogen per mu total for maize. Maize doesn't need as much fertilizer as wheat in my experience.

I irrigate maize twice — once at jointing in July, once at filling in August. If it rains enough, maybe only once. Water costs add up.

For labor, my wife and I do most of it. For wheat harvest, I hire the combine — it's 50 yuan per mu now, but no one can cut 3 mu by hand anymore. For maize, we usually harvest by hand still, or sometimes hire a small machine if my son is back to help. This year, I'll budget for hiring 3 days for wheat harvest help and 1 day for maize.

Total cost? Let me think... seed, fertilizer, water, pesticide, combine hire... probably around 1050 yuan for the year. That's a lot for us, but we have some cash saved from my son's remittances. I just hope the weather is good.

If things are normal, I expect about 420 kg per mu for wheat, and 500 kg per mu for maize. That's about what I got last year. Not great, not terrible. Good enough.
